newsitem.title: CHINA: China development bank mulls overseas debt issue.
newsitem.headline: China development bank mulls overseas debt issue.

text.p: China's State Development Bank, which issued a $330 million Yankee bond in January, is considering another bond offer in the second half of the year, a bank official said on Thursday.
"We are considering another international bond issue this year," the official said.
He said the offer still required approval from the State Planning Commission and the bank still needed to select domestic projects to make use of the funds.
The bank's 7.375 percent bonds due in 2007 were priced to yield 80 basis points over 10-year U.S. Treasury notes.
The State Development Bank plans to issue a similar Yankee bond this year, the Hong Kong based Sing Tao Daily quoted bank governor Yao Zhenyan as saying on Thursday.
The issue was planned because of brisk sales of the previous offer.

The bank said it would also continue to finance a number of key domestic projects including the massive Three Gorges dam, the 300,000-tonne ethylene project of Jilin Chemical Industrial Co Ltd and steelmaker Panzhihua.
